## Summary

A deterministic codemod had already wrapped every OpenAI/Anthropic client construction in this repo (`ai_scientist/llm.py`, `launch_scientist.py`, `experimental/launch_oe_scientist.py`, `review_iclr_bench/iclr_analysis.py`) with `router_runtime.py`, which transparently translates Chat Completions/Messages traffic to Router's `/v1/responses` when `RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY` is set, and falls back to the original provider otherwise. Its own `HANDOFF.md`/`REPORT.md` left 3 judgment calls open, plus I found one real bug blocking routing. I fixed all of it:

**Fixed so Router actually gets used:**
- **Removed `seed=0`** from the three `client.chat.completions.create()` calls in `ai_scientist/llm.py` (the `gpt` branch in both `get_response_from_llm`/`get_batch_responses_from_llm`, and the `o1`/`o3` branch). `seed` has no Responses-API equivalent, so Router's translator was rejecting every one of these requests as `Untranslatable` and silently falling back straight to OpenAI — meaning **no GPT call was ever actually reaching Router** despite the client being wrapped. I verified this against the Router simulator before and after: before, 0 requests reached the sim; after, `gpt-4.1` routed correctly (`POST /v1/responses model=gpt-4.1 valid=True`).
- **Added current Router-catalog Claude model ids** (`claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5`, sourced from the catalog the codemod fetched live via `GET /v1/models`) to `AVAILABLE_LLMS` in `ai_scientist/llm.py` and to the `--model` choices/dispatch in `review_iclr_bench/iclr_analysis.py`. Previously only the old dated snapshots (`claude-3-5-sonnet-2024...`) were selectable, and those aren't in Router's catalog, so Anthropic traffic could never route no matter what.
- **Moved the hardcoded `model="gpt-4o-2024-05-13"`** (4 call sites in `launch_scientist.py` and `experimental/launch_oe_scientist.py`, used for the post-writeup review step) into `DEFAULT_REVIEWER_MODEL = os.environ.get("AI_SCIENTIST_REVIEWER_MODEL", "gpt-4o-2024-05-13")` in `ai_scientist/llm.py`, so it's env-configurable instead of hardcoded at the call site. Default value unchanged.

**Verified:** compile/import check passes (10/10), and a live text-only request through the Router simulator succeeded end-to-end for `gpt-4.1` ("pong" back, `valid=True`).

**Could not migrate / left as-is, with reasons:**
- `llama3.1-405b` (`meta-llama/llama-3.1-405b-instruct` via OpenRouter) in `ai_scientist/llm.py` — not in Router's catalog; genuinely has no substitute, stays on OpenRouter directly.
- `deepseek-chat`/`deepseek-coder`/`deepseek-reasoner` and `gemini-*` branches — these construct `openai.OpenAI()` clients pointed at `api.deepseek.com` / `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` directly. The vendored runtime only intercepts `api.openai.com`/`api.anthropic.com` hosts, so this traffic never reaches Router; left untouched since Router doesn't proxy those hosts.
- `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` were **not deleted** from the README/env setup instructions. The vendored runtime's own design requires them to remain set: the SDK client constructors (`openai.OpenAI()`, `anthropic.Anthropic()`) raise immediately if unset, and they're also the fallback path for requests Router can't serve (e.g. the OpenRouter/DeepSeek/Gemini/Bedrock/Vertex branches above, plus any Router-side rejection). Deleting them would break imports and the fallback entirely, not just "Router-ineligible" calls.
- Hit an unrelated environment artifact during verification: the sandboxed `anthropic` SDK in this test env has a stub `Messages.create()` signature with no `temperature` parameter at all, so any Claude call (even against unmigrated `HEAD` code) throws `TypeError`. This is pre-existing and reproduces identically with the original, unmigrated code — not something introduced by this migration.
